tutorial.title: Grouping Values into Objects
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn how to access, use, and update object properties.

lessons.title: Intro
lessons.interactiveContent:
Let's say we have two variables, name and favoriteFood, which are both related to the same cat.

Make sure to pick name, followed by favoriteFood.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Two variables describe the same cat. Complete the names that match the cat's name and preferred food.

Make sure to pick name, followed by favoriteFood.

lessons.title: Grouping values into an Object
lessons.interactiveContent:
Instead of using two separate variables to describe our cat, we can group these into one variable, known as an object.

Make sure to pick cat.

lessons.title: Creating Objects
lessons.interactiveContent:
We create objects similarly to variables, with the keyword const followed by a name, an equal sign, and curly braces {}. Like const cat = {};.

Make sure to pick const followed by cat and then =, {}, ;.

lessons.title: Properties
lessons.interactiveContent:
The information inside an object is known as the object's properties. The properties go inside the object's curly braces {}.

Make sure to pick {, followed by name: "Garfield", and finally }.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The information inside an object is known as the object's properties.

Properties go inside the object's curly braces {}.

Complete the object with its name set to "Garfield".

Make sure to pick {, followed by name, :, "Garfield", and finally }.

lessons.title: Setting Properties
lessons.interactiveContent:
We create properties starting with a name, followed by a colon : and a value, like name: "Garfield".

Make sure to pick name, followed by :, and finally "Garfield".

lessons.title: Question: Creating Objects
lessons.interactiveContent:
What follows the equals sign when we create a new object?

Curly braces {}Parentheses ()

Curly braces {}.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You write const dog = and want an empty object. What completes the line?

Curly braces {}Parentheses ()Square brackets []

Make sure to pick Curly braces {}.

lessons.title: Example: Grouping values into an Object
lessons.interactiveContent:
Group the property into the cat object.

Make sure to pick { followed by name: and then "Garfield", }.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Group the cat's name property into the cat object.

Make sure to pick {, followed by name:, "Garfield", and finally }.

lessons.title: Question: Properties
lessons.interactiveContent:
What do we call the information contained within an object's curly braces {}?

The object's propertiesThe object's variables

The object's properties.
lessons.hardModeContent:
In const cat = { name: "Garfield" }, what is name: "Garfield" called?

An object propertyAn object variableAn object method

Make sure to pick An object property.

lessons.title: Question: Setting Properties
lessons.interactiveContent:
When we create a property, what do we put between the name and the value?

A colon :A comma ,

A colon :.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Complete the property name ? "Garfield". Which character replaces the question mark?

A colon :A comma ,An equals sign =

Make sure to pick A colon :.

lessons.title: Example: Creating Objects
lessons.interactiveContent:
Assemble the code to create an object.

Make sure to pick const followed by dog and then =, {, }, ;.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Create an empty object named dog.

Make sure to pick const, followed by dog, =, {, }, and finally ;.

lessons.title: Example: Properties
lessons.interactiveContent:
Create a dog object with property name: "Odie".

Make sure to pick const followed by dog and then =, {, name: "Odie", }.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Create the dog object with its name set to "Odie".

Make sure to pick const, followed by dog, =, {, name:, "Odie", and finally }.

lessons.title: Question: Grouping values into an Object
lessons.interactiveContent:
What do we call a group of related content grouped into one variable?

An objectA variable set

An object.
lessons.hardModeContent:
const pet = { name: "Odie" }; keeps related details in one variable. What is pet?

An objectA propertyA variable set

Make sure to pick An object.

lessons.title: Example: Setting Properties
lessons.interactiveContent:
Give the person the property name with value "Jon Arbuckle".

Make sure to type name: "Jon Arbuckle".

lessons.title: Adding a comma
lessons.interactiveContent:
To add more properties to an object, start with a comma, then add the property.

Make sure to pick ,, followed by nickname: "Tiger King".
lessons.hardModeContent:
To add more properties to an object, start with a comma, then add the property. Add nickname: "Tiger King" to person.

Make sure to pick ,, followed by nickname:, and finally "Tiger King".

lessons.title: Creating Multiple Properties
lessons.interactiveContent:
An object can have as many properties as we want, as long as each property is separated by a comma.

Make sure to pick ,, followed by ,.
lessons.hardModeContent:
An object can have as many properties as you want. Separate each property with a comma.

Complete the object with its occupation set to "Zookeeper".

Make sure to pick ,, followed by ,, occupation:, and finally "Zookeeper".

lessons.title: Property Types
lessons.interactiveContent:
Object properties can be numbers, strings, booleans, arrays, or even other objects.

Set the object age property to the number 57.

Make sure to type 57.

lessons.title: Displaying Objects
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can use console.log() to display the contents of our object person.

Make sure to pick console.log followed by ( and then person, ), ;.
lessons.hardModeContent:
We can use console.log() to display the contents of our object person. Log the whole object.

Make sure to pick console.log, followed by (, person, ), and finally ;.

lessons.title: Accessing Properties
lessons.interactiveContent:
We access an object's property using the object name, a ., and the property name, like person.nickname.

Make sure to pick person, followed by ., and finally nickname.
lessons.hardModeContent:
We access an object's property using the object name, a ., and the property name, like person.nickname. Print only the nickname value.

Make sure to pick person, followed by ., and finally nickname.

lessons.title: Updating Properties
lessons.interactiveContent:
After accessing a property value, we can update it using an equal sign. For example, try coding person.nickname = "Tiger Prince".

Make sure to type person.nickname = "Tiger Prince".

lessons.title: Question: Adding a comma
lessons.interactiveContent:
What goes between each property?

A comma ,Nothing

A comma ,.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Which character makes this object valid? { name: "Odie" ? age: 5 }

A comma ,A colon :An equals sign =

Make sure to pick A comma ,.

lessons.title: Question: Displaying Objects
lessons.interactiveContent:
What will console.log(myObject) display for the object myObject?

The Object and its propertiesOnly the name of the object

The Object and its properties.
lessons.hardModeContent:
const myObject = { color: "red" }; console.log(myObject); runs. What appears in the console?

The object and its color propertyOnly the text myObjectOnly the value "red"

The object and its color property.

lessons.title: Example: Adding a comma
lessons.interactiveContent:
Insert the missing comma between the object's properties.

Make sure to pick ,.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Separate the properties with a comma. Set occupation to "Animal Rights Activist".

Make sure to pick ,, followed by occupation:, and finally "Animal Rights Activist".

lessons.title: Example: Accessing Properties
lessons.interactiveContent:
Display the person object's occupation.

Make sure to pick person, followed by ., and finally occupation.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Read a property with the object name, a dot ., and the property name.

Display Animal Rights Activist from the person object.

Make sure to pick person, followed by ., and finally occupation.

lessons.title: Question: Accessing Properties
lessons.interactiveContent:
What do we put after the object name to access a property?

A period . and the property nameA question mark ?

A period . and the property name.
lessons.hardModeContent:
To read the name stored in person, which expression is correct?

person.nameperson:nameperson=name

Make sure to pick person.name.

lessons.title: Example: Property Types
lessons.interactiveContent:
Add a boolean property.

Make sure to pick true.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Add the active property as a boolean that says this person is active.

Make sure to pick active:, followed by true.

lessons.title: Question: Updating Properties
lessons.interactiveContent:
What symbol do we use to update an object's property to a new value?

The equals sign =The plus sign +

The equals sign =.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Complete the update person.name ? "Odie". Which symbol changes the property's value?

The equals sign =A colon :The plus sign +

Make sure to pick The equals sign =.

lessons.title: Example: Multiple Properties
lessons.interactiveContent:
Give this object an additional property.

Make sure to pick ,, followed by nationality:, and finally "USA".
lessons.hardModeContent:
Add nationality: "USA" after the occupation, then log the completed object.

Make sure to pick ,, followed by nationality:, "USA", and finally person.

lessons.title: Question: Creating Multiple Properties
lessons.interactiveContent:
How many properties can an object have?

As many as we wantNo more than 5

As many as we want.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A person object already has six properties. Can you add a seventh property?

Yes, objects can have as many properties as needed.No, objects stop after five properties.No, an object can only store one value type.

Yes, objects can have as many properties as needed.

lessons.title: Example: Displaying Objects
lessons.interactiveContent:
Display the contents of the person object using console.log.

Make sure to type console.log(person);.

lessons.title: Question: Property Types
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which types of information can be grouped into an object as its properties?

Numbers, strings, booleans, arrays, and even other objectsOnly strings and numbers

Numbers, strings, booleans, arrays, and even other objects.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Which object can validly group different kinds of information as properties?

{ name: "Odie", age: 5, active: true }Only an object whose properties are all strings.Only an object whose properties are all numbers.

{ name: "Odie", age: 5, active: true }.

lessons.title: Example: Updating Properties
lessons.interactiveContent:
Change the person object's name to "Barole Caskin".

Make sure to pick person followed by . and then name, =, "Barole Caskin", ;.
lessons.hardModeContent:
To update a property, access it with a dot, then use = followed by the new value.

Change the person object's name to "Barole Caskin" with an assignment.

Make sure to pick person, followed by ., name, =, "Barole Caskin", and finally ;.
